sections.overview: The Small White is a widespread day-flying butterfly whose caterpillars use many wild and cultivated plants, especially cabbages and their relatives.
sections.identification: The adult is white with dark tips on the forewings; males usually have one dark forewing spot and females two. The green caterpillar has a yellow dorsal line.
sections.habitat: It occurs in open and disturbed places, including gardens, meadows, crop fields, woodland edges and fallow ground.
sections.diet: Adults take flower nectar, while caterpillars feed mainly on Brassicaceae such as cabbage, turnip, rape and wild mustards; capers are also reported as a host plant.
sections.behavior: In suitable climates it may produce several generations in a year; a French field guide records up to four. It overwinters as a chrysalis in some regions.
sections.reproduction: Females lay eggs on host plants, where the caterpillars develop before pupating; the number of generations varies with region and season.
sections.ecology: It is a close relative of the Large White, P. brassicae, but is generally smaller; it also resembles P. napi and other white pierids, so wing markings help separate them.
sections.conservation: It is common across much of its range, although local abundance and the number of generations depend on conditions.
